source.title: Semantic Convergence: Investigating Shared Representations Across Scaled LLMs
source.authors: Daniel Son; Sanjana Rathore; Andrew Rufail; A. Simon; Daniel Zhang; S. Dave; Cole Blondin; Kevin Zhu; Sean O'Brien

record.file_problem: None; the text is readable, with some PDF line-break artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE-based feature comparison to Gemma-2 models with a fourfold size difference and reports cross-model feature-alignment results, extending indirect LLM evidence about SAE-derived features to this setting.
record.gate_note: The study measures alignment between SAE-derived features and semantic subspaces in two Gemma models. It does not test toy-model superposition, capacity competition, neuron-level polysemanticity, or whether SAE features are complete and canonical. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study takes pretrained Gemma Scope-style SAEs as a given decomposition and measures how well SAE feature spaces align across Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B (SVCCA/RSA after correlation matching). This is cross-model feature universality. It never tests whether the models hold features in superposition, whether SAEs recover those features, or whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical within a model. It never compares against neuron-level bases or other dictionaries. The SAE premise is relied on, not tested, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim that early layers represent multi-token subspaces more than single-token ones. They say this challenges the assumption that models encode single-token concepts, though it rests on one subspace. They also say the distance metric (Pearson, cosine, Euclidean) did not change results significantly.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares SAE-derived feature spaces and semantic subspaces across LLMs using correlation matching, SVCCA, and RSA; it does not use the toy-network superposition setup or test feature competition.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment varies with layer, matching strategy (1-to-1 versus many-to-1), filtering non-concept features, and the selected semantic subspace.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE feature spaces of Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B align far above random pairings. Peak 1-to-1 SVCCA is 0.73 (2B L14 vs 9B L19), against random means of 0.005–0.034. Alignment is strongest in middle layers and weak at early and late layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model universality of SAE-derived feature spaces across model scale, strongest in middle layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Semantic-subspace alignment depends on concept pairing. Emotion+Time and Nature+People reach about 0.62–0.63 SVCCA, while Country+People scores 0.03 against a random mean of 0.13. A multi-token Emotion+Time subspace aligns at 0.27–0.53.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model alignment of SAE semantic subspaces varies with concept combination, and multi-token concepts align in early and middle layers.

record.problems: Only Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B are studied, both using the same tokenizer. The authors cite resource constraints, analyze a limited number of semantic subspaces, and test only one multi-token subspace. The study compares SAE-derived features but does not independently validate their completeness or canonical status.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
All: no capacity or importance analysis.
All: no analysis of the origins of polysemanticity.
Whether features are spread across neurons, and whether SAEs recover sparse features. SAEs are assumed to yield monosemantic features.
Completeness, within-model stability and canonicity of SAE features. Only cross-model alignment of feature spaces is measured.
Dimensionality of features. The multi-token result concerns token span, not feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked every row to V4 and labelled it supports/limits_scope, but universality of SAE features across models does not test whether superposition or SAE-recoverable features exist. It also does not test whether SAE features are canonical units within a model. Several rows (r14, r15) describe the study's own filtering method. Captions contain inconsistencies: the Table 2 layer description and the Table 3 'bad pairs' label. No code is stated; this is a preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more sparse features than dimensions, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, and sparsity-dependent transitions or geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
The study analyzes SAE-derived features but does not independently establish that they are complete recoveries of the models’ features, or measure feature distribution across neurons.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the models’ representations.
Whether the features involved in superposition are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B vs Gemma-2-9B
rows.operation_detail: Compared 1-to-1 correlation-matched SAE feature spaces using SVCCA.
rows.baseline: Randomly paired feature scores; overall mean random SVCCA spans 0.005–0.034
rows.note: The peak is reported for the specified layer pair.
rows.check: Cross-model SVCCA of SAE feature spaces measures universality, not whether LLMs contain SAE-recoverable sparse features (V4). It cannot show the V4 effect.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B vs Gemma-2-9B
rows.operation_detail: Measured activation correlations for matched features before filtering non-concept features.
rows.value: Peak 0.70 at L22 and L39; mid-layer block average 0.60 ± 0.07
rows.note: The paper reports both a peak and a mid-layer average.
rows.check: Activation correlation of matched features between models. No baseline is stated; this is a universality measure.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B vs Gemma-2-9B
rows.operation_detail: Removed features classified as unimportant before calculating activation correlation.
rows.note: The text says middle-layer correlation becomes more evident after filtering.
rows.check: An effect of the study's own filtering step on its alignment score. This is method behaviour, not a version result.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B vs Gemma-2-9B
rows.operation_detail: Removed unimportant features and compared surrounding random matches.
rows.note: The authors state that filtering makes strong alignments clearer.
rows.check: A drop in correlation for random matches after filtering. This describes the method, not the phenomenon.
